headline: Pilandok Exits PAR as Habagat Continues to Affect Western Luzon
seoTitle: Pilandok Exits PAR September 3, 2026 | FMB News
seoDescription: Tropical Storm Pilandok exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility early September 3 while southwest monsoon rains continued over parts of western Luzon.
deck: The storm moved out of the Philippine monitoring area without a direct landfall threat, but monsoon rainfall remained a concern.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Tropical Storm Pilandok, internationally named Krovanh, exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility at about 4:30 a.m. on September 3, PAGASA said.
At 4 a.m., the storm was estimated about 1,030 kilometers east-northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon and was moving northwestward.

sections.heading: What the exit means
paragraphs: Pilandok was not expected to directly affect the country, and its exit ended the domestic cyclone-monitoring phase for the system.

sections.heading: Habagat remains
paragraphs: The southwest monsoon continued to bring rain to western parts of Luzon even after Pilandok moved outside PAR, so flood and landslide risks did not end with the storm's departure.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Cyclone exit and local weather risk are different things. Communities in saturated areas still needed to follow rainfall, river and marine advisories after Pilandok left PAR.
